Hi Tom — thanks for the screenshot, and sorry for the confusion.

Short answer: Chili Piper/Calendly sometimes auto-detects timezone from the browser or cookie state and that can flip if someone in your org previously used the same machine with a different tz. Two practical workarounds we use: 
- Use the scheduling link with an explicit timezone param (Calendly supports ?tz=Europe%2FLondon).
- If the widget still looks wrong, I can send a manual calendar invite (ICS) with the confirmed London time so it’s unambiguous.

Would 15:00 GMT on Wed (Mar 24) work? If so I’ll send the invite directly to avoid any further auto-detect issues. Note: DST transitions this month (US switches earlier than UK) have caused mismatches on a few demos — we double-check offsets for cross-region meetings the week of DST.

Options: 
1) I send a manual invite for 2026-03-24 15:00 GMT (recommended)
2) You try the Calendly link with tz param: https://calendly.com/redwood-inference/demo?tz=Europe%2FLondon
3) We use an alternate scheduler (Chili Piper) and I’ll verify the tz before confirming.

If you want, I’ll copy Marissa (AE) to handle the booking and follow-ups.

Best,
Camila Reyes
